# `docker_unused_images`

`docker_unused_images` removes the Docker images that no container uses,
running or stopped, as `docker image prune` does. It frees disk space on a
node whose old images fill it. `remove` says which images go: only those
without a name (`dangling_images_only`), or every image that no container
uses (`every_image_no_container_uses`).

An image is dangling when it has no name left: a pull of a tag that moved to
a newer image takes the tag from the old image, and a build that reuses a
tag does the same. [`docker_image`](docker_image.md) pulls images and
removes none.

## Set up

Docker must be installed on the node, and the node's Docker daemon must be
running, as for [`docker_image`](docker_image.md#set-up).

## Inputs

- `remove` (`dangling_images_only` or `every_image_no_container_uses`; required): no default: dangling_images_only removes the images that have no name left, such as the one a pull of a moved tag replaced (docker image prune); every_image_no_container_uses also removes named images that no container uses (docker image prune --all), such as a previous version that a deploy keeps for a quick rollback

## Outputs

The node task's result holds these fields. A later node task reads them as `.node_tasks.<id>.<field>`, where `<id>` is the node task's `id`.

- `status`
- `change`
- `reason`
- `value.removed_images`
- `value.freed_bytes`

## What a dryrun reports

Removes nothing; lists the images that a run would remove, each with its image_id, names, and size_bytes, as docker image inspect reports them; freed_bytes is null, because only the Docker daemon's removal says what it frees; unchanged when no image qualifies; not_checked while the docker command or the Docker daemon is missing.

## Retries and time limits

Bounded automatic retries by default; retry: false turns them off.

The node task takes the time limits `time_limit` and `time_limit_per_try`; without them, the project's `node_task_defaults` apply. `mmx describe-module task` describes the settings every node task accepts.

## Examples

### Remove the images that lost their names

```yaml
- docker_unused_images:
    remove: dangling_images_only
```

On the node, MMX lists the images without a name (`docker image ls
--filter dangling=true`) and leaves out each one that a container uses,
running or stopped (`docker container inspect`). If at least one unused,
unnamed image remains in the list, MMX asks the node's Docker daemon to
remove unused, unnamed images. MMX sends the request that
`docker image prune` sends. MMX reports the images the daemon deleted and
the bytes the daemon freed:

```text
changed — removed 3 images from the node's Docker images and freed 512.4 MiB (537291776 bytes): sha256:0e5c...; sha256:9a1f...; sha256:44d2...
```

`value.removed_images` lists each image with its `image_id`, its `names`,
and its `size_bytes` as `docker image inspect` reports it, and
`value.freed_bytes` holds the bytes that the daemon freed. When no image
qualifies, the node task is `unchanged` and asks the daemon nothing.

### Every image that no container uses

```yaml
- docker_unused_images:
    remove: every_image_no_container_uses
```

The example node task also removes named images that no container uses,
like `docker image prune --all`. For example, the node task removes
`registry.example.com/shop/web:2.3` after the containers moved to `2.4`.

**Running the example node task deletes a previous image kept for a quick
rollback when no container uses the previous image.** The
`every_image_no_container_uses` choice deletes the previous version during
the node task's run, after containers stop using the previous image. A
rollback must then pull the previous image again. Use
`dangling_images_only` on such a node, or remove the images only after the
new version has proved itself.

## How it works

- **The removal** is the daemon's own: MMX sends `POST /images/prune` with
  the filter `dangling=true`, or `dangling=false` for every image, on the
  daemon's Unix socket, which is what `docker image prune` sends. The
  daemon's answer, in JSON, gives the bytes it freed, counted by layer, so a
  layer that a remaining image shares is not counted. Which of the listed
  images went, MMX reads from `docker image ls` afterwards.
- **Images without a name.** The containerd image store, which a new
  installation of Docker 29 uses, keeps a record without a name for an
  image that a pull of a moved tag replaced, also when other records still
  give the same image names; `docker image ls --filter dangling=true` lists
  it. Prune removes only that record and the image stays, so the node task
  leaves such an image out.
- **Images that a container's name names.** The containerd image store also
  keeps an image whose name is the one a container was created with, such
  as `registry.example.com/shop/web:2.4` after a pull moved that tag to a
  newer image while the container still runs the older one. The node task
  leaves such an image out there too; the classic image store removes it.
- **A dryrun** removes nothing. It lists the images that a run would remove,
  with their sizes as `docker image inspect` reports them, which count
  shared layers in full. Only the daemon's removal says what it frees, so
  `freed_bytes` is `null` in a dryrun, and a later node task that reads the
  value is not checked.
- **Images from Docker's former builder.** A build without BuildKit leaves
  unnamed parent images. The daemon removes them with the image that needed
  them, and keeps an image that a used image still needs, taking only its
  name. The result lists the images of the listing that went, and says when
  the daemon removed only names or images that the listing did not name.

## Errors and what they mean

| The reason holds | What the error means, and what to do |
|---|---|
| `docker_unused_images.remove is required` | Validation requires `remove`; there is no default. |
| `the Docker daemon refused to remove unused images: a prune operation is already running` | Another Docker prune operation is running. Run the node task again when the Docker prune operation finishes. |
| `the docker command reaches the Docker daemon at ...` | MMX asks the daemon on a Unix socket of the node only. |

## Tested on

**Distributions:** Debian 12 and 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Rocky Linux 9, AlmaLinux 10.

The suite `tests/integration/docker_containers.py` pulls images whose tags
move and leaves one image in use by a stopped container. The suite compares
the dryrun, the run, and `docker image ls` on the node with
`dangling_images_only` and `every_image_no_container_uses`. The suite covers
Debian 12 and 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04, Rocky Linux 9, and AlmaLinux 10. The
[validation record](../../changing-mmx/validation.md) has the latest results.

## Why it works this way

- **`remove` has no default.** Whether named images are removed determines
  whether a rollback image survives, so each node task must specify the
  removal choice through `remove`.
- **The daemon's request, not the docker command's text.** `docker image
  prune` prints its result as text and rounds the bytes; the daemon's answer
  is JSON with the exact bytes.
- **`freed_bytes` counts layers, not images.** The sum of the removed
  images' sizes would count every shared layer, which stays on disk.
